repo.name: Dispatcher
repo.tagline: Takes transfer offers, keeps the booked schedule

kinds.actor: a person, system or schedule outside the apps
kinds.platform: a transfer platform the apps read or act on

link_kinds.act: an action back on a platform
link_kinds.reply: an answer going back to a person
link_kinds.off: exists but is switched off or not served

status.works: implemented end to end in the code, no stub markers (not run)
status.partial: implemented with a known gap, or switched off
status.unknown: cannot be told from the repository

groups.name: Catch new offers
groups.summary: Workers watch three platforms and take every offer that fits the rules.

groups.name: Steer the workers
groups.summary: The operator starts, stops and tunes the workers from a Telegram chat.

groups.name: Collect the booked schedule
groups.summary: Every 10 minutes each configured platform is read for transfers already booked.

groups.name: Run it on a server
groups.summary: Build the images, ship them with Ansible, and watch the server.

elements.name: Operator's chat
elements.summary: A person in an allowed Telegram chat who gets order messages and steers the workers.
how: Two separate bots: one manages the workers, one answers schedule requests.
Each bot answers only chats whose ids are listed in its config.

elements.name: Admin at a terminal
elements.summary: Whoever builds the images and runs the Ansible playbooks.
how: Root npm scripts wrap the playbooks: deploy-dispatcher, deploy-consolidator, deploy-registry, deploy-monitoring.
A dev container with Ansible and Node is provided for running them.

elements.name: Timers
elements.summary: Schedules inside the apps that start work without anyone asking.
how: Fetch delay per worker: 20 s by default, editable from Telegram.
Schedule round: every 10 minutes.
Transfeero session refresh: every 3 minutes.
Clean-up of past blocked hours: every 10 minutes.

elements.name: Offer mailbox
elements.summary: The Gmail inbox where Connecto sends its offers.
how: Read over IMAP with a user and password from config.
The inbox is opened read-only; mails are never marked or moved.

elements.name: Controller API
elements.summary: The central system that receives orders. It is not in this repository.
how: Only one call is used: POST /addOrders with a list of orders.
Address and API key come from each app's config.

elements.name: The server
elements.summary: The Linux host that everything is deployed to.
how: One host plays both roles in the inventory: app server and image registry.

elements.name: Welcome Pickups
elements.summary: Platform with a live worker; its bookings are read from the site's own JSON list.
how: Floor 1: unassigned transfers are polled and fitting ones get a driver assigned.
Floor 3: asks for assigned upcoming transfers of the next 2 days.

elements.name: Transfeero
elements.summary: Platform with a live worker; its bookings are read by replaying the site's own request.
how: Floor 1: new rides are polled and fitting ones accepted.
Floor 3: opens 'upcoming rides', captures the request the page makes, and sends it again.

elements.name: Connecto
elements.summary: Platform with a live worker fed by e-mail; its bookings are read from the confirmed-transfers table.
how: Floor 1: offers arrive as e-mails with a link to the offer page.
Floor 3: signs in with e-mail, password and a PIN, then reads every page of confirmed transfers.

elements.name: AtoB Transfer
elements.summary: Bookings are read from the upcoming-bookings table, then each booking is opened for details.
how: The table gives id, date, route, vehicle; each booking page adds client name, phone, price, passengers.

elements.name: Kiwitaxi
elements.summary: Bookings are read by re-sending the site's own data request, asking only for scheduled orders.
how: Opens the orders page, captures the GraphQL request it makes, changes the status filter to 'scheduled' and sends it again.

elements.name: City Airport Taxis
elements.summary: Bookings are read from the site's search endpoint, then each one is opened for details.
how: Each booking page adds client name, phone, vehicle type and net rate.
When the page is flagged 'doubled' (three sections) the net rate is halved.

elements.name: Shuttle Spain
elements.summary: Bookings are caught from the data the services page loads by itself.
how: Opens the services list and listens for the site's own 'get all services' answer.

elements.name: Google Sheet
elements.summary: Bookings kept by hand in a spreadsheet, read through a Google service account. No browser involved.
how: Reads 100 rows at a time from a start row until a short page comes back.
Which column means what (date, time, from, to, price, passenger…) is a template in config.

elements.name: Talixo
elements.summary: Bookings are read from the jobs table, but no booking id is read.
how: Reads date, time, from, to, vehicle and price from each table row.
watch_out: The order id is a random string made up on every read.

elements.name: World Transfer
elements.summary: Bookings are read from the driver app's Confirmed tab; ids are placeholders.
how: Signs in with a 'GTU' code, user and password; reads the cards; logs out.
watch_out: Signs in on every round — cookie reuse is commented out.
The order id is a random number, marked 'to be replaced' in the code.

elements.name: Elife
elements.summary: Bookings are caught from data the page loads while each ride is opened in turn.
how: Scrolls until 'no more items', opens every ride tile, and collects the ride data the page fetches.
watch_out: The 'already signed in?' check is a stub that always says no, so it signs in every round.
OpenMyRides.ts is kept in the package but its call is commented out.

elements.name: Chofix
elements.summary: Newest platform. Bookings are read from the confirmed-rides table, without an id.
how: Reads date, time, route, passengers, vehicle, price and the comment tooltip from each row.
watch_out: The order id is the literal text 'unknown' (marked todo).
Debug prints are still in the table reader.

elements.name: Polls for open offers
elements.summary: Asks Welcome Pickups and Transfeero, again and again, for offers nobody has taken yet.
how: Runs every fetch delay: 20 s unless changed from Telegram.
A poll that fails is retried (5 in the code), then skipped until the next tick.
Welcome Pickups: the site's JSON list of unassigned upcoming transfers, next 14 days, first 100.
Transfeero: the site's own 'new rides' request, captured from the page and sent again.
must_hold: The request is made from inside the signed-in browser page, so it only works while the session is alive.
change_here: How far ahead Welcome Pickups looks: filter.days default in WPickupsWorker.ts.
Retry count and pause: nextAction in CommonWorker.ts.

elements.name: Reads emailed Connecto offers
elements.summary: Finds new Connecto mails in the inbox, opens the link inside, and reads the offer.
how: Every fetch delay: looks for mail from Connecto newer than the last one handled.
Four kinds, told apart by subject: Transfer voucher, Transfer proposal, New Transfer, Transfer Available.
Opens the link from the mail in the browser and reads from, to, date, vehicle and price.
An offer whose page says it expired is skipped.
must_hold: The time of the last handled mail is saved, so a mail is handled once — even if taking it fails.
On its very first start the worker only notes 'now'; older mail is ignored.
change_here: How each mail kind's link is found: the extract… functions in ConnectoWorker.ts.
watch_out: The page is also checked for 'Transfer cancellation', but nothing uses that flag.

elements.name: Decides if an offer fits
elements.summary: Compares each offer with the operator's rules. Only a fitting offer is taken.
how: Welcome Pickups: not cancelled; driver's cost at least the minimum for a minivan or sedan (any other vehicle never fits); cost per km at least the minimal rate.
Transfeero: start or end contains 'Alicante'; payout at least the minimal order cost; vehicle class is in the configured vehicle map.
Connecto: some line of the accept list matches — same from, same to, vehicle contains, price at least.
All three: the pickup time must be outside every blocked window.
must_hold: A fitting offer is taken without asking anyone.
A misfit is reported, never taken.
change_here: Each platform's rule is one function: transferCompliance in WPickupsWorker.ts and ConnectoWorker.ts, rideCompliance in TransfeeroWorker.ts.
The 'Alicante' test is written into TransfeeroWorker.ts.
The numbers themselves are changed from Telegram — floor 2.

elements.name: Acceptance rules
elements.summary: Per worker: fetch delay, blocked hours, minimal costs, and Connecto's accept list.
how: Saved as a file in each worker's storage folder; survives restarts.
Defaults: delay 20 s, no blocked hours, minimal order cost 10000.
Welcome Pickups defaults: 1000 per vehicle, rate 100 per km, 14 days ahead.
Connecto default: an empty accept list, so nothing fits until one is uploaded.
must_hold: Blocked hours are stored as UTC instants; the bot shows and reads them in local time.
change_here: Defaults: BasicWorker.ts (common), WPickupsWorker.ts and ConnectoWorker.ts constructors.

elements.name: Assigns driver and car
elements.summary: Takes a Welcome Pickups transfer by assigning one of the company's drivers and a vehicle on the site.
how: Opens the transfers page and the transfer's 'Assign driver' dialog.
Picks a random driver who is not on the configured exclude list, and the first vehicle offered.
Clicks assign and waits up to 10 s for the site to confirm.
Then checks that the transfer shows up among the assigned ones. The whole sequence is tried up to 5 times, with a screenshot on failure.
must_hold: It gives up when no driver is left after exclusions or no vehicle is offered.
change_here: Drivers never to pick: driversToExclude in the worker's config.
Driver choice (random) and vehicle choice (first): AssignDriver.ts, AssignVehicle.ts.

elements.name: Accepts the Transfeero ride
elements.summary: Takes a Transfeero ride: opens it, picks the vehicle, clicks accept, waits for the site's answer.
how: Opens the ride's page; waits out Transfeero's 'Security Check' room if it shows up.
Passes the Cloudflare checkbox (up to 10 s).
Selects the vehicle that the config maps to the ride's class.
Clicks accept and waits up to 10 s; only an answer with status 200 counts as taken.
Every stage is timed in the log.
change_here: Which of your vehicles answers which ride class: vehicleTypeMap in config. A class missing from the map never fits.
Oldest first or newest first: processingOrder in config.
watch_out: GetSemiCompliantRideDate.ts exists in the package but nothing calls it.

elements.name: Clicks accept on offer
elements.summary: Takes a Connecto offer by pressing the accept control on the offer page that is already open.
how: Proposal mails use the 'accept proposal' control; the other three kinds use the page's success button.
watch_out: After the click it only waits half a second; nothing checks that the site confirmed.

elements.name: Order
elements.summary: The one record that every platform's offer or booking is turned into.
how: Carries id, platform, pickup time, from, to, car type, passengers, cost, traveler (name, phone, comment).
Has a type: compliant (fits, taken or already booked) or non-compliant (misfit).
Platform extras ride along: distance, commission, payment method, flight number.
must_hold: Pickup time is meant as a UTC instant; each platform converts from its own date format using the current UTC offset (+1 or +2).
change_here: The fields: Order.ts. How a platform fills them: its mapToOrder function.

elements.name: Announces orders in chat
elements.summary: Tells the chats bound to a worker about every new order.
how: Three marks: green for taken, yellow for 'does not fit', red for 'failed to accept'.
Shows id, pickup time, route, distance, car type, cost; traveler and passenger count only on taken orders.
More than 10 misfits in one batch become a single summary line.
Only chats bound to that worker get the message; with no bound chat nothing is sent.
change_here: Wording and fields: formatOrder in TelegramManageBot.ts.
watch_out: Writing the message adds the UTC offset to the order's pickup time in place, once per bound chat — and the same order object is handed to the publisher right after. Read from the code, not run.

elements.name: Publishes orders to controller
elements.summary: Sends orders to the central controller over HTTP.
how: POST to the controller's /addOrders with the list of orders and an API key header.
Floor 1: every new order, taken or misfit, as it appears. Failed accepts are not sent.
Floor 3: the whole schedule after every round.
must_hold: A send that fails is logged and dropped: no retry, no queue.
change_here: Address and key: the controller section of each app's config file.

elements.name: Keeps the session signed in
elements.summary: Gets each platform's page into a signed-in state and keeps it there.
how: Loads saved cookies, opens the platform, and looks whether it lands on the working page.
If not, it types the e-mail and password from config into the login form and saves the fresh cookies.
Transfeero worker: repeats the check and re-captures its requests every 3 minutes.
Cloudflare's checkbox is clicked by position; Transfeero's 'Security Check' room is waited out for up to 60 s.
Floor 3 wipes all cookies before each platform, then loads that platform's saved ones.
must_hold: Logins come only from the config file, never from the repository.
watch_out: The Welcome Pickups worker clicks the Cloudflare box once a second only while the worker is stopped — as written.
The Connecto worker never signs in; it only opens the links from its mails.

elements.name: Drives a real Chrome
elements.summary: Does every click and request through a real Chrome browser running in its own container.
how: Connects to a Chrome container by the address in config (10 tries, 3 s apart).
Floor 1: one Chrome per worker, so sessions never mix. Floor 3: one Chrome for all platforms.
Worker pages run at 1600×1024 in the Rome time zone with a 10 s default timeout.
Uses a patched Puppeteer build and a mouse-event fix so the sites see an ordinary browser.
Each container can show its screen over VNC, and keeps its Chrome profile in a volume.
must_hold: Every worker name in config needs a Chrome address under the same name, or start-up fails.
change_here: Which Chrome a worker uses: the browsers section of the dispatcher config, and the compose file.
watch_out: If Chrome disconnects it is only logged; nothing reconnects until the app restarts.

elements.name: Starts and stops workers
elements.summary: Creates one worker per config entry and remembers which ones are running.
how: Three worker types exist: wpickups, transfeero, connecto. Several workers may share a type — the compose file runs three Chrome containers for Transfeero.
Running yes/no is saved per worker; after a restart the running ones start again by themselves.
Start and Stop come from the Telegram menu (floor 2).
Passes each worker's new orders and accept failures on to the chat and the controller.
must_hold: An unknown worker type in config stops the app at start.
change_here: A new platform with live taking = a new case in WorkersManager.ts plus a worker package under packages/components/.
watch_out: In --dev mode only workers already marked running are set up, and the manage bot is not started.

elements.name: Lets in known chats only
elements.summary: Ignores Telegram messages from chats that are not on the allowed list.
how: Allowed chat ids come from the bot's config.
Four commands: /config, /worker, /restart_app, /reboot_host.
watch_out: Button presses are routed without that check in this repo's code. The base bot class is in an outside package, so whether it filters them is unverified.

elements.name: Binds chat to a worker
elements.summary: /worker <name> makes this chat talk to one worker, and hear from it.
how: An unknown name is answered with the list of available workers.
A chat with no binding quietly uses the first worker in config.

elements.name: Chat-to-worker binding
elements.summary: Which Telegram chat belongs to which worker.
how: Saved as a file; survives restarts.
Used twice: to pick the worker a chat's menu controls, and to pick the chats that get a worker's order messages (floor 1).

elements.name: Shows the worker menu
elements.summary: /config opens a button menu for the worker this chat is bound to.
how: Top screen: worker name, running or stopped; buttons Start, Stop, Fetch delay, Filter.
Filter: time exclusions and minimal order cost.
Welcome Pickups adds a cost per vehicle and a per-km rate. Connecto swaps cost for 'order details' — its accept list.
After a button asks for a value, the next message from that chat is taken as the answer.
change_here: Common screens: CommonBotComponent.ts. A platform's extra screens: its own BotComponent file.
watch_out: On Welcome Pickups, the Back button shown after a wrongly typed rate points at a misspelt menu id and does nothing.

elements.name: Changes the rules
elements.summary: Turns what the operator typed or uploaded into new rules for the worker.
how: Fetch delay: a number of seconds.
Blocked hours: 'HH:MM-HH:MM DD.MM' in local time, one day at a time. Removed by number: 1, 1-3 or 1,3,5.
Minimal order cost: a number; on Welcome Pickups one per vehicle, plus a per-km rate.
Connecto accept list: a text file with one 'from - to - vehicle - price' per line. It replaces the whole list and can be downloaded back.
must_hold: A value that does not parse changes nothing and is answered with an error.
A change is saved at once and is used from the next poll.

elements.name: Forgets past blocked hours
elements.summary: Every 10 minutes removes blocked windows whose end has passed.
how: Runs only while the worker is running.

elements.name: Restarts app or server
elements.summary: Two commands that end the running app from the chat.
how: /restart_app: the app exits with code 2 and Docker's restart policy brings it back.
/reboot_host: runs the system's reboot command from inside the app.
watch_out: In the shipped deployment the app runs in a container; whether 'reboot' there reaches the host is unverified.

elements.name: Answers schedule requests
elements.summary: The second Telegram bot: /services, /collect <platform>, /collect_all.
how: Replies 'Collecting...' first, and the schedule when it is ready.
Answers only chats on its own allowed list.

elements.name: Runs collection rounds
elements.summary: Starts a full round by itself every 10 minutes, and on request.
how: The next round starts 10 minutes after the previous one ends.
One round at a time: a request that arrives mid-round waits for it and gets its result.
A result younger than 60 s is reused for requests.
A request for one platform re-reads just that one and keeps the rest.
must_hold: After every round, full or single, the whole kept schedule is published again.
change_here: The 10 minutes and the 60 seconds: BackgroundConsolidator.ts.

elements.name: Visits platforms one by one
elements.summary: Goes through the configured platforms in order, in one browser.
how: Before each platform all browser cookies are wiped.
A platform that errors is tried up to 3 times, with a screenshot on each failure.
Pickups already in the past are dropped.
One platform failing does not stop the others: its slot holds the error.
change_here: A new platform: a case in ConsolidatorService.ts, a config type in ConsolidatorConfig.ts, and a package under packages/components/.

elements.name: Reads booked transfers
elements.summary: Signs in to one platform and turns its list of booked transfers into orders.
how: Every platform package has one 'get assigned transfers' action that returns orders.
Asking the site's own data endpoint from inside the page: Welcome Pickups, Transfeero, Kiwitaxi, City Airport Taxis.
Catching the data the page itself loads: Elife, Shuttle Spain.
Reading the HTML table or cards: Connecto, Talixo, AtoB, World Transfer, Chofix.
Google Sheet needs no browser.
must_hold: Every booking is marked compliant: it is already yours.
change_here: How one platform is read: its package's GetAssignedTransfers.ts.
watch_out: Four of twelve have gaps: Talixo, World Transfer and Chofix give no real booking id; Elife and World Transfer sign in on every round.

elements.name: Latest schedule
elements.summary: What the last round found: per platform, either its upcoming bookings or the error.
how: Kept in memory only; empty after a restart until the first round ends.

elements.name: Writes the schedule message
elements.summary: Turns the schedule into Telegram messages sorted by pickup time.
how: Platforms that failed are listed first.
Each booking shows platform, id, pickup time, from, to, vehicle, price.
Covers the first two calendar days that have bookings, with a rule between days.
Split into messages of at most 4000 characters.
watch_out: It shifts pickup times to local time inside the kept schedule itself, so a second request within the 60-second reuse shifts them again. Read from the code, not run.

elements.name: Prepares a fresh server
elements.summary: One playbook that makes a bare Linux host ready for the apps.
how: Installs base packages; creates the app user and folders.
Adds the registry's hostname to /etc/hosts and trusts its certificate.
Installs Docker Engine and the Compose plugin.

elements.name: Keeps the app images
elements.summary: A private Docker registry on the server, with TLS and a password.
how: A script makes a self-signed certificate, valid 10 years.
The playbook installs the registry with basic auth and an optional web UI on port 5010.

elements.name: Builds the app images
elements.summary: Compiles each app and bundles it into one JavaScript file inside a small Node image.
how: Two stages per app: build all workspace packages and bundle with Rollup, then copy the single bundle into a slim image.
A private npm token is needed at build time for the 'dispatcher-commons' package, which is not in this repository.
Images are tagged for the private registry.
watch_out: Root scripts bundle-dispatcher and bundle-consolidator call 'npm run build', which the root package.json does not define.
README says the bundle script also pushes the image; no tracked script pushes.
README still describes packages/launcher and lerna; the code is apps/dispatcher and pnpm. The code wins.

elements.name: Ships an app to server
elements.summary: A playbook per app: write its config, pull its image, start it next to its Chrome containers.
how: Writes the app's config file from an Ansible variable and templates the compose file.
Logs in to the registry, pulls the latest image, starts the stack.
If the config changed, the app container is recreated.
The dispatcher ships with five Chrome containers, the consolidator with one.
watch_out: The role docker-stack is not used by any playbook and points at a compose file that is not in the repository.

elements.name: Config and secrets
elements.summary: Everything private: platform logins, bot tokens, chat ids, controller address and key, Chrome addresses.
how: One config file per app, read once at start; never in git.
On the server it is written from Ansible variables that are also git-ignored.
must_hold: A config change takes effect only after the app restarts.

elements.name: Runs the workers
elements.summary: The dispatcher app: everything on floors 1 and 2 runs inside this one process.
how: Start order: storage, config, manage bot, then each worker's Chrome and the workers that were running.
The UTC offset (+1 or +2) is worked out once at start from daylight-saving time.
Started with --dev it skips the manage bot and only sets up workers already marked running.
watch_out: After a daylight-saving switch the old offset stays until the app restarts.
test/test.ts is a scratch file of manual experiments, not a test suite.

elements.name: Runs schedule collection
elements.summary: The consolidator app: everything on floor 3 runs inside this one process.
how: Start order: storage, config, the one browser, the schedule bot, then the first round.
watch_out: test/test.ts is a scratch file that reads one platform by hand, not a test suite.

elements.name: Collects metrics and logs
elements.summary: A monitoring stack beside the apps that gathers host numbers, container numbers and container logs.
how: Logs: Promtail tails the app and Chrome containers into Loki.
Metrics: node-exporter (host) and cAdvisor (containers) into Prometheus.
Both keep 30 days.
watch_out: The log filter names chrome-transfeero-1 and -2 but not -3.
App-level metrics are planned: the scrape entries for the two apps are commented out.

elements.name: Shows dashboards
elements.summary: Grafana on port 3001 with two ready-made dashboards.
how: Server Overview: CPU, memory, disk, network, load, uptime, containers, app logs.
Container Metrics: per-container CPU, memory, network, disk, restarts, plus Chrome panels and logs.
In the Ansible deployment only Grafana is open to the outside by default.

elements.name: Sends logs to Telegram
elements.summary: A log bot that would post app logs and failure screenshots to a Telegram chat. Switched off.
how: Both apps have the lines that start it commented out; the latest commit is 'disable tg logger'.
Logs now go to the console only, and from there into Loki.
Screenshots are still taken on failures, into a local file.
watch_out: Whether the stand-in logger does anything with those screenshots is unverified — its class is in an outside package.

elements.name: Answers health checks
elements.summary: Each app image declares a health check against a local /health address that nothing serves yet.
how: The images probe port 9091 (dispatcher) and 9092 (consolidator).
No tracked code listens on those ports.
The Prometheus entries for the same ports are commented out 'until app metrics are added'.
watch_out: Unverified: the outside 'dispatcher-commons' package could open such a port; nothing in this repo asks it to.

links.label: app images
links.note: unverified: no tracked script pushes the images

routes.name: Take a Welcome Pickups transfer
routes.summary: A transfer that fits the rules gets one of your drivers assigned, with nobody clicking.
step_notes: Every fetch delay (20 s by default) the worker asks the site for unassigned upcoming transfers: next 14 days, first 100.
Every transfer in the answer is checked on every poll.
It fits when it is not cancelled, the driver's cost reaches the minimum for a minivan or sedan, the cost per km reaches the minimal rate, and the pickup is outside all blocked hours.
No one is asked. A fitting transfer is taken straight away.
On the site: open 'Assign driver', pick a random driver who is not excluded and the first vehicle, click assign, wait for the OK, then verify. Up to 5 tries.
The transfer becomes an order marked compliant, with the traveler's name and phone.
Every order a worker reports goes to the chat side.
Chats bound to this worker get pickup time, route, distance, car, traveler and cost.
The same order goes to the controller side.
The order is posted to the controller's addOrders address. A failed send is only logged.

routes.name: Take a Transfeero ride
routes.summary: A new ride that fits the rules is accepted with the right vehicle, with nobody clicking.
step_notes: Every fetch delay the worker re-sends the site's own 'new rides' request from inside the page.
Every ride in the answer is checked on every poll.
It fits when the pickup is outside blocked hours, start or end contains 'Alicante', the payout reaches the minimal order cost, and the vehicle class is in the configured vehicle map.
Fitting rides are taken one after another; config can reverse their order.
On the site: open the ride, pass the security room and the Cloudflare box, select the mapped vehicle, click accept, wait up to 10 s. Only status 200 counts.
The ride becomes an order marked compliant, with the customer's note as comment.
Every order a worker reports goes to the chat side.
Chats bound to this worker get pickup time, route, distance, car, passengers and cost.
The same order goes to the controller side.
The order is posted to the controller's addOrders address.

routes.name: Take a Connecto email offer
routes.summary: An offer that arrives by e-mail and matches the accept list is accepted on Connecto's page.
step_notes: Every fetch delay the worker looks in the inbox for Connecto mail newer than the last one it handled.
It pulls the link out of the mail, opens it in the browser and reads from, to, date, vehicle and price. Expired offers are skipped.
Each offer is judged once.
It fits when the pickup is outside blocked hours and a line of the uploaded list has the same from, the same to, a vehicle name the offer contains, and a price the offer reaches.
No one is asked.
The accept control on the open offer page is pressed. Nothing checks afterwards that the site confirmed.
The offer becomes an order marked compliant. Connecto orders carry no traveler details.
Every order a worker reports goes to the chat side.
Chats bound to this worker get pickup time, route, car and cost.
The same order goes to the controller side.
The order is posted to the controller's addOrders address.

routes.name: Report offers that don't fit
routes.summary: An offer that fails the rules is left alone, but the operator and the controller still hear about it.
step_notes: From a poll — or, for Connecto, from a mail.
It is not taken. It becomes an order marked non-compliant. Welcome Pickups and Transfeero remember, in memory, which ones they already reported.
Misfits go the same way as taken orders.
Without traveler details. More than 10 misfits at once become one summary line.
Misfits are published too.
Posted with its type set to non-compliant.

routes.name: Report a failed accept
routes.summary: When taking a fitting offer goes wrong, the operator gets a red message so a person can step in.
step_titles: A fitting offer is being taken
step_notes: Shown here for Transfeero; the other two platforms behave the same.
The site says no, a step times out, or a control is missing.
The offer is still turned into an order, so the message can show it.
Failures go to the chat side only.
A failed order is not sent to the controller. Welcome Pickups and Transfeero try again on the next poll; a Connecto mail is handled only once.

routes.name: Stay signed in
routes.summary: Workers log in by themselves and keep their sessions, so polling never needs a person.
step_notes: Each worker has its own Chrome, with its own profile.
Cookies from the last successful sign-in are put back into the browser.
It opens the platform; if that does not land on the working page it types the login from config and saves the new cookies. Transfeero repeats this every 3 minutes.

routes.name: Resume workers after restart
routes.summary: After the app restarts, the workers that were running start again without anyone pressing Start.
step_notes: Running yes/no is saved for every worker.
10 tries, 3 s apart. If a Chrome cannot be reached the app exits.
Workers marked running sign in and begin polling; the others wait for Start.

routes.name: Point chat at a worker

step_notes: Only chats on the allowed list are answered.

From now on this chat's menu controls that worker, and that worker's order messages come here.

routes.name: Start or stop a worker
routes.summary: Two buttons in the /config menu switch a worker's polling on and off.
step_notes: Only chats on the allowed list are answered.
The menu opens as a message with buttons.

Start signs in first, so it can fail; the error text is then shown. The new state is saved and survives restarts.
'Worker started' or 'Worker stopped', with a Back button.

routes.name: Change the fetch delay
routes.summary: How many seconds a worker waits between two polls.
step_notes: Only chats on the allowed list are answered.
The menu shows the current delay and asks for a new one.
The next message from this chat is read as the number.
The very next wait already uses it.

routes.name: Block out hours
routes.summary: Time exclusions: windows in which no offer fits, whatever its price.
step_notes: Only chats on the allowed list are answered.
The menu lists the current windows in local time.
Format 'HH:MM-HH:MM DD.MM', local time, one day at a time. Remove by number: 1, 1-3 or 1,3,5.
Offers with a pickup inside the window stop fitting from the next poll.
Every 10 minutes, while the worker runs, windows that have ended are removed.

routes.name: Set the minimal order cost
routes.summary: The price below which an offer does not fit.
step_notes: Only chats on the allowed list are answered.
Transfeero: one number. Welcome Pickups: one per vehicle (minivan, sedan) and a separate per-km rate. Connecto has no such screen.
Anything that is not a number is refused.
Used from the next poll.

routes.name: Upload Connecto accept list
routes.summary: The list of routes, vehicles and lowest prices that Connecto offers are accepted against.
step_notes: The chat must be bound to a Connecto worker.
Shows how many entries the list has; offers Upload and Download.
One line per entry: 'from - to - vehicle - price'. A line that does not parse rejects the whole file.
The new list replaces the old one entirely.

routes.name: Restart the app
routes.summary: /restart_app ends the dispatcher process so that it starts fresh.
step_notes: Only chats on the allowed list are answered.
The bot answers 'Restarting application' and the process exits with code 2.
The container's restart policy brings the app back; workers that were running resume (floor 1).

routes.name: Reboot the server
routes.summary: /reboot_host asks the operating system to reboot.
step_notes: Only chats on the allowed list are answered.
The bot answers 'Restarting server' and runs the system's reboot command.
The shipped app runs inside a container. Whether a reboot issued there reaches the host cannot be told from the repository.

routes.name: Prepare a new server
routes.summary: One playbook turns a bare Linux host into one that can run the apps.
step_notes: From the ansible folder.
Base packages, app user and folders, the registry's name and certificate, Docker Engine with Compose.

routes.name: Host the image registry
routes.summary: A private, password-protected place on the server for the two app images.
step_titles: Make a certificate, run the playbook
step_notes: 'generate-certs' makes a self-signed certificate; 'deploy-registry' installs the registry with TLS, basic auth and a web UI.
The playbook waits until the registry answers.

routes.name: Build the app images
routes.summary: Each app is compiled and bundled into one file inside a Docker image named for the private registry.
step_notes: The compose file of each app has a build section. The root 'bundle' scripts call a 'build' script the root package.json does not define.
Unverified: the images are tagged for the registry, but no tracked script pushes them.

routes.name: Ship the dispatcher
routes.summary: One playbook puts the dispatcher app and its five Chrome containers on the server.
step_notes: npm run deploy-dispatcher.
From a git-ignored Ansible variable holding the whole config as JSON.
After logging in to the private registry.
The app plus Chrome for wpickups, transfeero-1, -2, -3 and connecto. The app is recreated when its config changed.
One per worker, by the addresses in config.

routes.name: Ship the consolidator
routes.summary: One playbook puts the schedule app and its single Chrome container on the server.
step_notes: npm run deploy-consolidator.
From a git-ignored Ansible variable.
After logging in to the private registry.
The app plus one Chrome. The app is recreated when its config changed.
One browser for all platforms.

routes.name: Watch server and logs
routes.summary: Dashboards for the host, every container, and the apps' logs.
step_titles: App logs and numbers flow in
step_notes: The playbook uploads the configs and dashboards and starts six monitoring containers.
Container logs are tailed; CPU, memory, network and disk are measured per container and for the host.
Their logs as well — except chrome-transfeero-3, which the log filter does not name.
Metrics in Prometheus, logs in Loki.
Port 3001: 'Server Overview' and 'Container Metrics'.

routes.name: Look inside a browser
routes.summary: Every Chrome container can show its screen over VNC, to watch or to click by hand.
step_notes: Ports 5901 to 5905 for the workers' Chromes, 5910 for the schedule one. Off by default in the Ansible deployment, on in the local compose files.

routes.name: Run it in dev mode
routes.summary: Starting the dispatcher with --dev runs the workers quietly, without the Telegram manage bot.
step_notes: The manage bot is not started, and only workers already marked running are set up. They still need reachable Chrome addresses.

routes.name: Send logs to Telegram
routes.summary: A log bot for posting logs and failure screenshots to a chat. It is switched off in both apps.
step_notes: The lines that start the log bot are commented out; logs go to the console and on to Loki.

routes.name: Expose app health and metrics
routes.summary: A /health address and app metrics are prepared for in the images and the monitoring config, but not served.
step_notes: Port 9091 for the dispatcher; nothing in the repository listens there.
Port 9092. The matching Prometheus entries are commented out until app metrics exist.
